permit.exempt_list_quote: 105.2. Work exempts from permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of the code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of the code or other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction. Permits shall not be required for the following: (a) Building permits shall not be required for the following: (i) One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, if the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet, 11 square meters. (ii) A fence that is not more than 7 feet, 2-meters-134-millimeters, high. (iii) Oil derricks. (iv) A retaining wall that is not more than 4 feet, 1,219 millimeters, in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding class I, II, or III-A liquids. (v) A water tank supported directly on grade if the capacity is not greater than 5,000 gallons, 18,925 liters, and the ratio of height to diameter or width is not greater than 2 to 1. (vi) A sidewalk and driveway not more than 30 inches, 762 millimeters, above adjacent grade and not over any basement or story below and are not part of an accessible route. (vii) Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops, and similar finish work. (viii) Temporary motion picture, television, and theater stage sets and scenery. (ix) Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a group R-3 occupancy [...] (x) Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes, not including service systems. (xi) Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached 1- and 2-family dwellings. (xii) Window awnings in group R-3 and U occupancies [...] (xiii) Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters, and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches, 1,753 millimeters, in height. [(b) electrical, (c) mechanical and later items follow]
permit.source_note: This is the state rule R 408.30409 (Michigan Building Code section 105.2 as amended; history 2024 AACS), which Detroit enforces. R 408.30406a (section 105.1) reads: 'Owners or their authorized agents shall obtain the required permit from the building official before undertaking any construction, enlargement, alteration, repair, relocation, demolition, change of occupancy [...] regulated by the code.' Detroit's own guidance ('Do I Need a Building or Trade Permit?', https://detroitmi.gov/sites/detroitmi.localhost/files/2025-12/Do%20I%20NEED%20A%20PERMIT.pdf) could not be opened; a search excerpt of BSEED's FAQ says 'it is unlawful to perform construction work on a structure in the City of Detroit without first obtaining a permit'.
permit.note: The list names 'cabinets, countertops, and similar finish work' and 'nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters, and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches'. Toilet partitions or compartments are not named; the only partitions named are nonfixed, movable ones.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Detroit job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material and see the Michigan rules that apply in Detroit.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Detroit offices, schools, auto plants and hospitals, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Michigan's plumbing rules set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. They apply across the state, Detroit included. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Michigan's building rules, which Detroit enforces, list the work that needs no building permit. The list covers painting, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work, and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high that aren't fixed in place. It doesn't name toilet partitions. Ask Detroit's building department (BSEED) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.install_rule: Detroit licenses and registers contractors for certain construction work each year, so confirm with the city's Buildings, Safety Engineering and Environmental Department (BSEED) whether partition installation is covered. Michigan licenses residential builders and maintenance and alteration contractors, but has no state license for commercial interior work such as partition installation. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: Detroit registers contractors for certain construction work, so ask BSEED whether your installer's work is covered.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** on schools and other public buildings paid for in whole or in part by the state, Michigan law requires at least the prevailing local wage and benefits, and contractors on those jobs must register with the state. The Wayne County schedule dated November 2025 lists a journeyman carpenter at $74.81 an hour at straight time. The state issues new rates every November 1.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 6% in Detroit. Michigan has one statewide rate and no city or county sales tax.
page.buyers_extra: - **Stadiums, casinos and event venues:** HDPE or phenolic where crowds and nightly washdown are hard on stalls, stainless steel in premium public restrooms.

page.official_names: - The rules by their official names: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design; Michigan barrier free design requirements (1966 PA 1, MCL 125.1351 to 125.1356; 2021 Michigan Building Code Chapter 11; ICC A117.1-2017 except sections 611 and 707); 2021 Michigan Building Code (2021 International Building Code with Michigan amendments, R 408.30401 to R 408.30499a), effective April 9, 2025; 2021 Michigan Plumbing Code (2021 International Plumbing Code with Michigan amendments, R 408.30701 to R 408.30796), effective March 12, 2024; both apply statewide under the Stille-DeRossett-Hale Single State Construction Code Act (1972 PA 230, MCL 125.1508a) and are enforced in Detroit by BSEED; Section 105.2 of the building code (R 408.30409) for work exempt from permits; NFPA 286 for HDPE.
